question: What rebates are available for a heat pump?
html:
Heat Pump Rebates in Our Area

We don't have a verified list of current heat pump rebates or their dollar amounts, so we won't quote figures that could be wrong. Rebates depend on your utility, your county, the equipment you choose and what you heat with today. Our team can check what applies to your home during an estimate.

What decides your rebate

  • Your electric utility. Many utility programs set their own rules and amounts.
  • Your current heating fuel. Some programs treat a switch from oil or propane differently from a gas or electric upgrade.
  • Equipment efficiency. Higher-rated systems often qualify for more.
  • Timing. Program funds and rules can change during the year.

For tax credits, please ask a tax professional. We can't advise on eligibility.

Why it matters locally

Many homes we serve still heat with fuel oil or propane. These homes are often the ones asking about heat pumps. About 241k core Central PA households heat this way, and about 390k do across all 13 counties we serve (Punctual Pros market profile).

CountyShare heating with oil or propane
Perry44.5%
Lebanon37.6%
Berks30.0%
Adams27.7%
Lancaster25.2%

Source: Punctual Pros market profile. Ocean and Monmouth counties in NJ are different. There, 78-81% of homes use utility gas.

Housing age matters too. Across the core territory, 45-64% of homes were built before 1980 (Punctual Pros market profile). Older systems are often the ones due for replacement.

What we'd need to answer fully

To give exact amounts, we would need:

  • Current rebate schedules from each electric utility in our footprint.
  • Any state program terms for Pennsylvania and New Jersey.
  • Qualifying equipment lists matched to the models we install.

That's roughly 241k core-PA oil and propane homes (Punctual Pros market profile), and clear, accurate rebate answers are what turn a heat pump question into a booked replacement in that base.

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Build and date-stamp a rebate reference by utility and state for all 13 counties. Assign an owner to refresh it each quarter.
  2. Add a rebate check to the estimate workflow so technicians confirm eligibility on site.
  3. Create a heat pump conversion offer for oil and propane homes in Perry, Lebanon, Berks, Adams and Lancaster.
  4. Track rebate-assisted jobs separately so conversion rates can be measured against the growth plan (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
